'''''Senecio barbertonicus''''', the '''Barberton groundsel'''<ref name='ucr'>{{cite web|url=http://www.gardens.ucr.edu/events/shrubsFall.html |title=SHRUBS |access-date=2008-02-27 |author=The Friends of U.C. Riverside Botanic Gardens |author-link=University of California, Riverside, Botanic Gardens |date=2007-10-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060909155116/http://www.gardens.ucr.edu/events/shrubsFall.html |archive-date=September 9, 2006 }}</ref> 
or '''succulent bush senecio''',<ref name='Carruthers'>{{cite book
 | last = Carruthers
 | first = Vincent
 | title = The Wildlife of Southern Africa: A Field Guide to the Animals and Plants of the Region
 | orig-year = 2005
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=QygFIjP9jYUC
 | access-date = 2008-02-27
 | year = 2005
 | publisher = Struik
 | isbn = 1-86872-451-4
 | pages = 310 pages
 | chapter = Wild Flowers
 | chapter-url = https://books.google.com/books?id=QygFIjP9jYUC&pg=PT248
}}</ref> is an evergreen [[succulent]] shrub of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asteraceae]] and [[genus]] ''[[Senecio]]'', native to [[Southern Africa]],<ref name='sabonet'/> named after one of its native localities [[Barberton, Mpumalanga|Barberton]] and is now also being cultivated elsewhere for its [[drought tolerance|drought resistance]], clusters of sweetly scented,<ref name='Carruthers'/> golden-yellow, tufted flower heads in winter and attractiveness to butterflies,<ref name='ucr'/> the [[Vanessa cardui|painted lady]] butterfly (''Vanessa cardui'') in particular.<ref name='smgrowers'>{{cite web
 | url = http://www.smgrowers.com/products/plants/plantdisplay.asp?plant_id=3121
 | title = ''Senecio barbertonicus'' - Succulent Bush Senecio 
 | access-date = 2008-02-27 
 | work = San Marcos Growers Web Site
}}</ref>

== Description ==
A succulent bush growing over {{convert|6|ft|m|sigfig=1|order=flip|abbr=on}} tall and wide with a fleshy trunk, light green, cylindrical, finger-like leaves {{convert|2|to|4|in|cm|0|order=flip|abbr=on}} in length and {{convert|1/4|to|3/8|in|mm|0|order=flip|abbr=on}} in diameter, densely packed around the stem and curved at the base to lie parallel to the stem and pointing upwards.<ref name='sntc'>{{cite web
 | url = http://www.sntc.org.sz/flora/speciesinfo.asp?spid=3331
 | title = ''Senecio barbertonicus'' Klatt
 | access-date = 2008-02-27
 | work = Swaziland's Flora Database
 | publisher = South African National Botanical Institute (PRECIS database) and the Swaziland National Herbarium
 | archive-date = 2011-05-16
 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110516100738/http://www.sntc.org.sz/flora/speciesinfo.asp?spid=3331
 | url-status = dead
 }}</ref>

The fragrant yellow flowers, {{convert|3/8|in|cm|0|order=flip|abbr=on}} wide and {{convert|3|in|cm|0|order=flip|abbr=on}} long, bloom July through September,<ref name='Carruthers'/> are terminal and produce seeds with a dense tuft of bristles.

''Senecio barbertonicus'' is hardy to at least {{convert|25|°F|°C|order=flip}}.<ref name='smgrowers'/>

== Distribution ==
''Senecio barbertonicus'' grows predominantly in rocky grassland and [[bushveld]] in [[Southern Africa]] in areas ranging from [[Swaziland|Eswatini]] and [[Mozambique]], to Eastern parts of [[Zimbabwe]] and [[South Africa]]<ref name='Carruthers'/> at elevations between {{convert|110|and|5500|ft|m|order=flip|abbr=on|sigfig=2}}.<ref name='afpd'>{{cite web
 |url        = http://www.ville-ge.ch/cjb/bd/africa/details.php?langue=an&id=98011
 |archive-url = https://archive.today/20130116043122/http://www.ville-ge.ch/cjb/bd/africa/details.php?langue=an&id=98011
 |url-status   = dead
 |archive-date = 2013-01-16
 |title      = ''Senecio barbertonicus'' Klatt
 |access-date = 2008-02-27
 |work       = African Flowering Plants Database
 |publisher  = Conservatoire et Jardin botaniques de la Ville de Genève and South African National Biodiversity Institute, Pretoria
}}</ref>

It is locally common in protected areas in eastern, central, and southwestern Eswatini<ref name='sabonet2'>{{cite web
 |url         = http://www.sabonet.org.za/downloads/35_swaziland_tree_atlas/b.swazi.aster-celastra.pdf
 |title       = SABONET Tree Atlas Report No. 38
 |access-date  = 2008-02-27
 |author      = The Southern African Botanical Diversity Network
 |work        = Swaziland Tree Atlas
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20081121021526/http://www.sabonet.org.za/downloads/35_swaziland_tree_atlas/b.swazi.aster-celastra.pdf
 |archive-date = 2008-11-21
}}</ref>
in [[Gauteng]], [[KwaZulu-Natal]], [[Limpopo]], [[Mpumalanga]] and [[North West (South African province)|North-West]].<ref name='afpd'/>
